projects.name: tinymachines.ai
projects.what: The front door, the documentation tree, the style guide and the roof's own API. Not a project in the sense the others are: it is the thing they arrive under.

surfaces.name: The main site
surfaces.what: The front page. Reached from the masthead rather than from the nav, because a nav entry for the page you are already on is noise.

surfaces.name: The documentation tree
surfaces.what: The written documentation, with its navigation built from the documents themselves.

surfaces.name: The style guide
surfaces.what: The guide and the widget zoo: every component, shown working.

surfaces.name: Admin
surfaces.what: Dev keys and the people they belong to. Deliberately not in the navigation: that is not security, the key the API demands is, but it is not a page a reader has any use for.

surfaces.name: The roof API
surfaces.what: What the pieces are and which of them are answering, spoken as REST and as MCP.

projects.what: A transistor-level MOS 6502 traced from die photographs, and everything built on it: the explorer, the API over the real chip, the warm engine process and the console.

surfaces.name: The explorer
surfaces.what: The die itself, lit by what it is doing, plus the measured tables and the primer. The die data is CC BY-NC-SA and is served from one place at both addresses, never copied.

surfaces.name: The 6502 API
surfaces.what: A transistor-level MOS 6502 over HTTP, one half-cycle at a time. The reference is here and checks itself against the running service, and since 2026-08-24 the service answers under this address too: each address gets a schema that names that address, so what you read is true for where you read it. The subdomain stays the primary name for now.
surfaces.status: here, and still on the subdomain

surfaces.name: Die Runner
surfaces.what: Die Runner: a console whose frames are run on the real die. The builder pages and the cartridge editor live beside it.

surfaces.name: The editor
surfaces.what: Claim a handle, edit your page, publish a ROM: the registry's writing half, signed in with your token.

surfaces.name: The registry
surfaces.what: Everyone publishing cartridges, and what they published. Read-only here: publishing happens in the editor.

surfaces.name: The halfwave lab
surfaces.what: A 6502, half a clock phase at a time. The research bench, and it stays one.

surfaces.name: The visual6502 archive
surfaces.what: visual6502.org recovered from the Wayback Machine, 174 MB of it: the wiki rebuilt from its wikitext and the die photography made browsable again. The overview is ours; the preserved pages keep their own design, because that is what a preservation is.

projects.name: hotbits
projects.what: True random bytes from the decay of a radioactive source: a Geiger counter on a Pi, with bits taken from the timing between decay events. The instrument still runs where it always has; what is here is the roof over it.

surfaces.name: The entropy gateway
surfaces.what: Keys and byte budgets in front of the TRNG. /v1/bytes needs a bearer token; /v1/seeds needs no key and cannot drain the pool. The open /random/* endpoints answer 410 and say why: the pool refills at a few dozen bytes a minute and was reachable by anyone. The gateway publishes its own schema at /v1/openapi.json, and the reference here reads both documents on that host.

surfaces.name: The Geiger TRNG
surfaces.what: The instrument itself, and what it has measured: the byte pool, the randomness batteries, long-term and diurnal series, incidents and sensors. Its landing page and its reference are here, generated from the schema it publishes and checked against what it answers.
